skill.name: detect-ai
skill.description: Analyze text for likely AI authorship using the HumanizerAI API and present a score, metrics, and recommendation.
skill.summary: Checks text for AI-writing signals with a HumanizerAI score and concise metrics.
skill.author: humanizerai

security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced examples, not executable shell code. The meaningful risk is intentional submission of user text to the HumanizerAI API. No hardcoded secret or prompt injection language was found.

remediation.issue: Submitted text is sent to a third-party detection API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending sensitive text and document HumanizerAI data handling expectations.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on an external API and service-specific key.
remediation.suggestion: Document the required HUMANIZERAI_API_KEY variable and avoid printing the key in errors or logs.

remediation.issue: Detection results can be misused as proof of authorship.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to treat scores as review signals and combine them with human judgment.

content.value_statement: AI-generated text can be hard to identify before submission or publication. This skill sends text to HumanizerAI and returns a clear score, metrics, and recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Accepts text supplied with the /detect-ai command.
Calls the HumanizerAI detection endpoint through WebFetch.
Reports score.overall as the main AI likelihood score.
Shows metrics such as perplexity, burstiness, readability, and n-gram score.
Suggests whether the text may need humanizing based on the score.
limitations: Requires a HumanizerAI API key in the environment.
Sends submitted text to a third-party API.
Detection scores are probabilistic and should not be treated as proof.
Results depend on HumanizerAI API availability and response format.

use_cases.title: Review Publication Drafts
use_cases.description: Screen articles, posts, and web copy before release to identify AI-writing signals.

use_cases.title: Check Academic Drafts
use_cases.description: Review essays or research summaries for AI-like patterns before sharing or submitting them.

use_cases.title: Assess Vendor Copy
use_cases.description: Evaluate submitted marketing text when policies require disclosure of AI-assisted writing.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Short Passage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for one paragraph or short response.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Article Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: /detect-ai Analyze this full draft for AI-writing signals. Focus on the overall score and strongest metrics: [paste draft]
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before publishing a longer draft.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Revision
prompt_templates.prompt: /detect-ai Analyze this revised text and tell me whether it still appears AI-generated: [paste revised text]
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether editing reduced AI-like signals.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Publication Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: /detect-ai Analyze this publication draft. Summarize the score, metrics, and risk of submitting it as human-written: [paste draft]
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for policy or editorial workflows.

output_examples.input: A short product description that sounds polished and repetitive.
output_examples.output: AI Detection Results: Score 78 out of 100, likely AI-generated. The recommendation is to revise sentence variety and add specific human context.

output_examples.input: A personal essay draft with uneven sentence length and concrete details.
output_examples.output: AI Detection Results: Score 24 out of 100, likely human-written. The recommendation is to keep the natural structure and review only for clarity.

output_examples.input: A mixed report section combining original notes with generated summary text.
output_examples.output: AI Detection Results: Score 55 out of 100, mixed signals. The recommendation is to inspect high-scoring sections and rewrite generic passages.

best_practices: Remove private or regulated information before running detection.
Treat the score as a review signal, not a final judgment.
Check the overall score together with metric patterns and context.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential customer, employee, or legal text without approval.
Do not accuse an author based only on one score.
Do not expose the API key in prompts, screenshots, or logs.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes supplied text for signals associated with AI-written content.

faq.question: Does it send text outside my workspace?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill posts the supplied text to the HumanizerAI detection API.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill expects HUMANIZERAI_API_KEY to be available in the environment.

faq.question: Is the score proof that text was AI-written?
faq.answer: No. The score is probabilistic and should be reviewed with context.

faq.question: Which score should I trust first?
faq.answer: The skill uses score.overall as the main AI likelihood score.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
